Report DescriptionINITIAL/FINAL INCIDENT TYPE: VESSEL MAJOR MARINE CASUALTY LOCATION: WOODS HOLE, MA TIME INCIDENT OCCURRED: 0856 EDT / 1256 Z TIME OF INITIAL REPORT TO NCC: 1445 EDT / 1845 Z NAME OF REPORTING UNIT: USCG SECTOR SOUTHEASTERN NEW ENGLAND AMPLIFYING INFORMATION: • ON JULY 17, USCG SECTOR SOUTHEASTERN NEW ENGLAND RECEIVED A MAYDAY CALL ON VHF CHANNEL 16 FOR THE MOTOR VESSEL (M/V) FAVOR, THAT WAS TAKING ON WATER AFTER RUNNING AGROUND NEAR WOODS HOLE, MASSACHUSETTS. • M/V FAVOR IS A JAMAICAN-FLAGGED, 127-FOOT LUXURY SUPERYACHT WITH TEN ADULTS AND THREE CHILDREN ONBOARD. • USCG SECTOR SOUTHEASTERN NEW ENGLAND ISSUED AN URGENT MARINERS INFORMATION BROADCAST (UMIB) AND LAUNCHED USCG STATION WOODS HOLE. • FALMOUTH FIRE DEPARTMENT AND TOW BOAT US WERE ALSO NOTIFIED AND RESPONDED TO THE SCENE. • FALMOUTH FIRE DEPARTMENT REMOVED SEVEN PASSENGERS WHILE THE SIX REMAINING CREW MEMBERS REMAINED ONBOARD TO SECURE THE FUEL LINES AND ASSESS THE DAMAGE TO THE YACHT. • THERE IS A REPORTED 4,000 GALLONS OF DIESEL ONBOARD. • THERE ARE NO SIGNS OF POLLUTION. • THERE IS A GASH TO THE PORT SIDE ENGINE ROOM OF THE VESSEL, AND THE PORT SIDE STABILIZER HAS BEEN RIPPED FROM THE YACHT. • MARINE SAFETY UNIT CAPE COD ASSESSED THE DAMAGES AS EXCEEDING $2,000,000, MAKING THIS SITUATION A MAJOR MARINE CASUALTY. • USCG STATION WOODS HOLE IS ENFORCING A 500-YARD SAFETY ZONE WHILE TOW BOAT US TOWS THE VESSEL TO FAIRHAVEN, MASSACHUSETTS, WHERE THE VESSEL WILL BE LIFTED OUT OF THE WATER FOR FURTHER DAMAGE ASSESSMENT. • USCG NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER STOOD DOWN THE CIC PROCESS WITH CONCURRENCE FROM BOTH AREA COMMANDS.

Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 10 gallons
AN EMPTY ROLL OFF CONTAINING RESIDUAL INCINERATOR ASH COLLECTED RAIN WATER. A LEAK IN THE SEAL TO THE ROLLOFF RESULTED IN ABOUT 5 TO 10 GALLONS OF THE ASH CONTAMINATED STORM WATER TO LEAK ONTO PAVEMENT. THE RELEASE PRIMARILY RESIDED ON PAVEMENT HOWEVER, THE LEADING EDGE OF THE RELEASE IMPACTED CRUSHED STONE AND UNDERLYING SOIL ADJACENT TO PAVEMENT.
